sources.title: Adaptive Precision Floating-Point Arithmetic and Fast Robust Geometric Predicates
sources.summary: Shewchuk constructs adaptive orientation and incircle predicates from floating-point expansions. The fast path evaluates ordinary floating-point expressions, estimates their error, and escalates only uncertain signs to higher precision.
keyFindings: Predicate correctness can be separated from coordinate construction so most geometry stays on the fast floating-point path.
The escalation threshold must derive from the executed arithmetic sequence and its error bound.
limitations: The paper supplies predicates, not a complete policy for repairing non-manifold meshes or resolving coincident contours.

usage.decision: Use the adaptive-predicate pattern for orientation, segment ordering, triangle-plane classification, and topology-changing decisions.

pdf.accessNote: Public author copy. Use for project research and cite the journal article.

sources.title: A Generic Solution to Polygon Clipping
sources.summary: Vatti describes a general scanbeam clipping algorithm for arbitrary polygons. Its event ordering and active-edge structure are relevant to contour union, difference, and offset cleanup.
keyFindings: A single clipping model can process concave polygons and holes when edge events and winding state remain explicit.
Topological output depends on deterministic event ordering at coincident vertices and horizontal edges.
limitations: The paper predates modern robust-predicate practice and does not define the degeneracy contract required by this project.

usage.decision: Evaluate the scanbeam model against a smaller arrangement-based implementation before choosing the production polygon kernel.

sources.title: Exact and Robust (Self-)Intersections for Polygonal Meshes
sources.summary: Campen and Kobbelt localize mesh intersections with an adaptive octree, then resolve critical cells with plane-based BSP operations under explicit precision bounds.
keyFindings: Broad localization limits exact work to cells that contain an intersection.
Input quantization and fixed-precision bounds can provide a documented correctness envelope.
limitations: The full BSP repair method is larger than the minimum viable slicer and may exceed the first implementation scope.

usage.decision: Adopt localization and explicit precision accounting. Defer the complete BSP repair operator until failure data justifies it.

pdf.accessNote: Public institutional copy. Cite the Computer Graphics Forum article.

sources.title: Maximizing Parallelism in the Construction of BVHs, Octrees, and k-d Trees
sources.summary: Karras maps sorted Morton codes to binary radix-tree nodes so each internal node can calculate its range and children independently. The construction exposes one parallel task per internal node.
keyFindings: Sorted spatial keys can encode hierarchy topology without a level-by-level construction pass.
The output layout and equal-key tie rule are part of the algorithm contract.
limitations: A linear BVH favors construction speed. Its traversal quality must be measured against the slicer's repeated layer queries.

usage.decision: Prototype this construction for GPU and CPU layer indexes, then retain it only if total build-plus-query time beats simpler z-interval buckets.

pdf.accessNote: Public author copy. Cite the High Performance Graphics paper.

sources.title: Distance Transforms of Sampled Functions
sources.summary: Felzenszwalb and Huttenlocher reduce a class of grid transforms to separable lower-envelope calculations. The Euclidean case executes linear work per dimension instead of searching every source cell.
keyFindings: A squared Euclidean distance transform can execute as independent one-dimensional passes over rows and columns.
The lower-envelope representation produces exact grid distances under the stated sampled-function model.
limitations: The transform operates on a discrete grid. Grid resolution and conservative rasterization still control geometric error.

usage.decision: Use as the reference algorithm for infill fields, clearance maps, and support influence fields on raster layers.

pdf.accessNote: Published under CC BY. Preserve attribution to both authors and the journal.

sources.title: A General Algorithm for Computing Distance Transforms in Linear Time
sources.publication: Mathematical Morphology and its Applications to Image and Signal Processing
sources.summary: Meijster, Roerdink, and Hesselink split exact Euclidean distance transformation into a vertical scan and an independent horizontal lower-envelope pass.
keyFindings: The two-phase data flow maps naturally to a structure-of-arrays grid and parallel row or column dispatch.
Intermediate integer squared distances avoid square roots until a consumer needs physical units.
limitations: The paper does not account for GPU threadgroup occupancy, transposition cost, or Apple unified-memory behavior.

usage.decision: Benchmark beside the Felzenszwalb–Huttenlocher formulation and choose one shared CPU/Metal contract.

pdf.accessNote: Public institutional copy. Cite the published chapter.

sources.title: Bridging the Gap: Automated Steady Scaffoldings for 3D Printing
sources.summary: Dumas, Hergel, and Lefebvre construct supports from vertical pillars and printable bridges. The optimization includes overhang contact selection and stability during intermediate print states.
keyFindings: Bridges convert unsupported spans into structures anchored at both ends.
Support validity depends on the evolving printed prefix, not only the final model geometry.
limitations: Printer-specific bridge limits and surface-quality tolerances require calibration before the method can become a default.

usage.decision: Use as the basis for an optional bridge-aware support planner after the simpler overhang and vertical-support pipeline is validated.

pdf.accessNote: Open repository copy. Cite the ACM Transactions on Graphics article.

sources.title: Clever Support: Efficient Support Structure Generation for Digital Fabrication
sources.summary: Vanek, Galicia, and Benes detect overhang samples, define printable support cones, and greedily merge nearby support branches into a tree.
keyFindings: Support-cone intersection turns printer angle limits into a concrete feasible region for branch merging.
The greedy merge produces practical tree supports but does not guarantee a global minimum.
limitations: The physical tests cover a specific printer, material, and parameter range. Those dimensions cannot transfer as universal defaults.

usage.decision: Adopt support cones and explicit printer calibration. Treat greedy tree merging as a benchmark candidate.

pdf.accessNote: Public academic copy with author and publisher notices intact. Cite the Computer Graphics Forum article.

sources.title: Support Slimming for Single Material Based Additive Manufacturing
sources.summary: Hu, Jin, and Wang optimize model orientation and deform geometry to reduce support demand while limiting shape change.
keyFindings: Support demand can be reduced before slicing by jointly changing orientation and local shape.
The method treats geometric deviation as an optimization constraint rather than a repair side effect.
limitations: HW Slicer must preserve imported geometry by default, so automatic shape deformation is outside the first product contract.

usage.decision: Use as background for orientation scoring and a possible explicit design-assistance mode. Do not mutate production input automatically.

sources.title: Single-Pass Parallel Prefix Scan with Decoupled Look-Back
sources.summary: Merrill and Garland use redundant local work to decouple block progress from global prefix propagation. Their scan reads each input and writes each output once in the steady data path.
keyFindings: A prefix scan can drive stream compaction and output allocation without a separate global-count pass.
Correctness depends on publication state, memory ordering, and forward-progress assumptions.
limitations: The implementation and evaluation target NVIDIA GPU execution. Metal synchronization and Apple GPU scheduling require a separate proof and benchmark.

usage.decision: Use the report as an algorithm candidate, not a direct port. Establish a two-pass Metal baseline first.

pdf.accessNote: Public technical report. Preserve the report number in citations.

sources.title: Simple, Fast, and Practical Non-Blocking and Blocking Concurrent Queue Algorithms
sources.publication: Proceedings of the Fifteenth Annual ACM Symposium on Principles of Distributed Computing
sources.summary: Michael and Scott define blocking and non-blocking FIFO queues around atomic pointer updates and explicit progress properties.
keyFindings: A queue algorithm must specify reclamation and atomic ordering together with its pointer transitions.
A two-lock queue can permit one enqueue and one dequeue to execute concurrently with a simpler proof.
limitations: The original machine model and memory-reclamation discussion do not directly specify ARM64 acquire-release operations.

usage.decision: Use for terminology and correctness review. Prefer bounded queues or ownership transfer before introducing a lock-free queue.

pdf.provenance: University of Rochester author publication archive
pdf.accessNote: Public author copy. Cite the PODC proceedings article.

sources.title: QuickCheck: A Lightweight Tool for Random Testing of Haskell Programs
sources.publication: Proceedings of the Fifth ACM SIGPLAN International Conference on Functional Programming
sources.summary: Claessen and Hughes express program properties as executable functions, generate structured random inputs, and reduce failures to smaller counterexamples.
keyFindings: Generators encode valid input structure while properties encode behavior independent of specific examples.
Failure reduction converts a random counterexample into a small regression fixture.
limitations: The paper uses Haskell. Odin requires an explicit generator, seed, shrinker, and replay interface.

usage.decision: Adopt property-based generation and deterministic shrinking for parsers, predicates, polygon operations, and scheduling invariants.

sources.title: Simplifying and Isolating Failure-Inducing Input
sources.summary: Zeller and Hildebrandt repeatedly partition a failure-inducing input, execute a controlled test, and retain the smallest subset or difference that preserves the failure.
keyFindings: A reducer needs a stable pass, fail, and unresolved result contract.
Automated minimization makes large parser or geometry failures suitable for permanent regression tests.
limitations: Non-deterministic failures break the test oracle and must be stabilized before reduction.

usage.decision: Build reducers for 3MF package parts, mesh components, layers, contours, and G-code command ranges.

pdf.accessNote: Public author copy. Cite the IEEE Transactions article.

sources.title: The NIST RS274NGC Interpreter, Version 3
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.summary: NISTIR 6556 specifies an RS274/NGC interpreter that parses blocks, maintains modal state, and emits canonical machining functions.
keyFindings: Parsing and machine action separate through a canonical-function boundary.
Modal groups and block execution order require explicit state transitions.
limitations: FFF printer dialects extend and diverge from RS274/NGC. Firmware-specific commands need separate profiles.

usage.decision: Adopt the modal-state and canonical-command architecture, then define explicit FFF dialect profiles.

pdf.accessNote: United States government report. Preserve report number and DOI.

sources.title: 3MF Core Specification, Version 1.3.0
sources.publication: 3D Manufacturing Format Core Specification and Reference Guide
sources.summary: The 3MF Core specification defines package relationships, model resources, meshes, components, units, transforms, and producer-consumer conformance requirements.
keyFindings: A 3MF reader must validate both ZIP package relationships and XML model constraints.
Units, transforms, component graphs, and resource identifiers must resolve before triangles enter the geometry pipeline.
limitations: Version 1.4.0 is the latest consortium revision. Version 1.3.0 remains the archived PDF baseline and requires a tracked delta review.

usage.decision: Implement version 1.3.0 as the initial conformance baseline, then audit the 1.4.0 source revision before declaring current-format support.

pdf.accessNote: Official specification copy. Preserve the embedded terms and version.

sources.title: Procedure Call Standard for the Arm 64-bit Architecture
sources.publication: Application Binary Interface for the Arm Architecture
sources.summary: AAPCS64 defines register roles, argument and result transfer, stack alignment, data layout, and obligations across separately compiled AArch64 routines.
keyFindings: Interop boundaries must preserve the platform register and stack contracts before Odin, C, Objective-C, and assembly can call one another safely.
Aggregate layout and homogeneous vector rules affect SIMD helpers and foreign-function bindings.
limitations: The PDF asset distributed with the 2025Q4 release is labeled 2025Q1 internally. The source tree identifies 2025Q4, so this discrepancy must remain visible.

usage.decision: Treat the standard as the ABI authority for all hand-written ARM64 and foreign-function boundaries.

pdf.accessNote: CC BY-SA 4.0 with the specification's patent grant and trademark terms.

sources.title: Metal Shading Language Specification, Version 4.1
sources.summary: Metal Shading Language 4.1 defines shader data types, address spaces, atomics, synchronization, function attributes, compilation, and compute-kernel execution rules.
keyFindings: Buffer ownership and address-space types must match the resource binding and synchronization plan.
Threadgroup barriers order only the memory domains and threads named by their contract.
limitations: Language availability does not prove feature support on a device. Runtime family checks must use the feature tables and Metal APIs.

usage.decision: Use as the language authority for every compute kernel and memory-order review.

pdf.accessNote: Reference copy from Apple. Retain Apple's notices and link to the current official download.

sources.title: Metal Feature Set Tables
sources.summary: The May 21, 2026 feature tables map Metal features, formats, limits, and programming models to Apple and Mac GPU families.
keyFindings: Kernel dispatch dimensions, buffer limits, atomics, and memory features must derive from the active GPU family.
Metal 4 language features and device features have separate availability conditions.
limitations: Apple updates this document independently of the repository. The checksum identifies the reviewed snapshot only.

usage.decision: Bind startup capability detection and test-matrix selection to these limits, while checking the live device through Metal APIs.

pdf.accessNote: Reference copy from Apple. Retain Apple's notices and link to the current official download.

sources.title: Odin Documentation
sources.summary: The official documentation defines Odin language syntax, package behavior, memory facilities, foreign imports, build modes, and platform integration.
keyFindings: Allocator choice and lifetime remain explicit at package boundaries.
Foreign bindings expose platform APIs without changing their ownership or ABI contracts.
limitations: The documentation changes continuously and has no immutable PDF edition. Code must pin the Odin compiler version separately.

usage.decision: Use as the language authority, with compiler behavior verified against the version pinned by the project toolchain.

sources.title: Notarizing macOS Software Before Distribution
sources.summary: Apple's distribution documentation defines the submission, status, ticket stapling, and Gatekeeper validation flow for software distributed outside the Mac App Store.
keyFindings: The release pipeline must sign the complete application before notarization and staple the accepted ticket to the distributed artifact.
Release verification must execute on the final packaged artifact, not on an earlier build directory.
limitations: The live documentation changes with Apple's service and toolchain. The release runbook must record the executed command versions.

usage.decision: Use when the release system is implemented. Keep signing identities and service credentials outside the repository.
